readmeHtml:
Agentation is an agent-agnostic visual feedback tool. Click elements on your page, add notes, and copy structured output that helps AI coding agents find the exact code you're referring to.

Install

npm install agentation -D

Usage

import { Agentation } from 'agentation';

function App() {
  return (
    <>
      <YourApp />
      <Agentation />
    </>
  );
}

The toolbar appears in the bottom-right corner. Click to activate, then click any element to annotate it.

Connect to your agent

Copied feedback works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Grok, or any AI tool. For direct sync, register npx -y agentation-mcp server with your MCP client and connect the toolbar to its HTTP endpoint:

<Agentation endpoint="http://localhost:4747" />

Keep the agent running, add a test annotation, and ask it to read the feedback. See the setup guide.

Features

  • Click to annotate – Click any element with automatic selector identification
  • Text selection – Select text to annotate specific content
  • Multi-select – Hold Cmd/Ctrl to select elements individually, or drag to select multiple at once
  • Area selection – Drag to annotate any region, even empty space
  • Animation pause – Pause supported CSS animations, Web Animations, and videos to capture specific states
  • Structured output – Copy markdown with selectors, positions, and context
  • Embedded pages – Select elements in open shadow roots and same-origin iframes
  • Integration options – Capture identifying attributes, choose metadata-only Copy formats, and open detected source locations through your editor integration
  • Hash routes – Opt in to separate annotations and sessions for each hash route
  • Dark/light mode – Toggle in settings, persists to localStorage
  • Zero dependencies – No runtime libraries beyond the React peer dependencies

See the package README for props and integration examples.

How it works

Agentation captures class names, selectors, and element positions so AI agents can grep for the exact code you're referring to. Instead of describing "the blue button in the sidebar," you give the agent .sidebar > button.primary and your feedback.

Requirements

  • React 18+
  • Desktop browser (mobile not supported)

Docs

Full documentation at agentation.com

License

© 2026 Benji Taylor

releases.name: Agentation 3.1.0
releases.body:
## Added

- Optional app names and Copy formats for source paths, CSS classes and identifying attributes.
- An Open in editor callback and `portalContainer` integration for host modals and popovers.
- Selection inside same-origin iframes, including nested frames.
- Opt-in hash routing and an option to disable global keyboard shortcuts.

## Improved

- Toolbar styles render inside Shadow DOM.
- Deep selection works through overlays and open shadow roots.
- Keyboard activation, accessible control names and focus return.
- Toolbar, panel, annotation editor and marker motion.

## Fixed

- Copy, Send and synchronization preserve feedback changed while operations are pending.
- Clear all completes with large batches; failed Copy and Send operations preserve feedback.
- Callback-only Send supports asynchronous delivery and failure handling.
- Popup placement, viewport edges, Safari spacing and zoom alignment.
- Iframe marker positioning and numbering, React 19 import compatibility and source-location filtering.
- Layout selection, persisted edits and resolved annotations after reconnecting.

[Full changelog](https://agentation.com/changelog#v3.1.0) · [API documentation](https://agentation

releases.name: agentation-mcp 1.3.0
releases.body:
- Preserve source locations, layout edits and annotation state during synchronization.
- Fix concurrent SQLite event sequencing.
- Improve reconnects and cancellation of watch requests.
- Bound retained event history and apply browser-origin rules consistently.
- Retry temporary webhook delivery failures.
- Correct the declared Node.js minimum to 20, matching the existing SQLite dependency requirement. Node.js 24 LTS is recommended.

[Setup and documentation](https://agentation.com/mcp)

aiSummary.oneLiner: An agent-agnostic visual feedback tool for providing structured UI context directly to AI coding assistants.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Agentation serves as a visual feedback tool that bridges the gap between what developers see on a webpage and the structured context AI coding agents need to modify it. It enables users to click any element on their rendered application and attach descriptive notes or requested changes directly to the UI component. The tool captures precise class names, selectors, and element positions without relying on external dependencies. It then generates structured markdown output containing this metadata, which can be effortlessly copied and provided to any AI coding assistant to locate the exact code requiring modification.
keyFeatures: Visual Element Selection: Allows users to click and select specific DOM elements directly on the page with automatic selector identification.
Animation Pausing: Freezes CSS, JavaScript, and video animations to easily capture and annotate specific dynamic application states.
Multi-element Selection: Enables dragging to select multiple elements at once or highlighting specific regions, including empty space.
Structured Markdown Output: Generates detailed context including exact selectors and positions that AI agents can easily grep.
Zero Dependency Architecture: Implemented using pure CSS animations without relying on heavy runtime libraries.

useCases.title: UI Bug Reporting
useCases.description: Developers use the tool to highlight visual bugs on a page and provide the exact context to an AI agent for a fix.

useCases.title: Iterative Design Tweaks
useCases.description: Designers attach notes to UI elements requesting styling changes, passing the structured output to an agent to implement the CSS.

useCases.title: Codebase Navigation for AI
useCases.description: Helping AI agents locate the exact source code responsible for rendering a specific visual component without manual searching.

useCases.title: Capturing Dynamic States
useCases.description: Pausing complex animations to instruct an AI assistant to modify the styling of a specific transition frame.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers and UI designers who utilize AI coding agents and need a highly precise method to communicate visual interface changes.
